scenario: Discussing weekend plans with a friend
frequency_note: words ranked ~300–700 by frequency of Korean

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 주말에 뭐 할 계획이야?
dialogue.translation: What are your plans for the weekend?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 영화 보러 가고 싶어. 같이 갈래?
dialogue.translation: I want to go see a movie. Do you want to go together?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 그 영화 재미있다고 들었어. 그런데 시간이 좀 없어.
dialogue.translation: I heard that movie is fun. But I don't have much time.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 그럼 토요일 오후는 어때?
dialogue.translation: Then, how about Saturday afternoon?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 토요일 오후에 시간이 돼. 좋은 생각이야!
dialogue.translation: I have time on Saturday afternoon. Good idea!

key_phrases.translation: What are your plans for the weekend?
Do you want to go together?

scenario: Returning a faulty item at a shop
frequency_note: words ranked ~300–700 by frequency of Korean

vocabulary.note: Used to exchange one product for another.
Common in purchase and refund contexts.
Necessary for returns.
Combines with 나다 (to occur).
Contrast with 헌것 (used).
Polite way to apologize, more formal than 미안하다.
Used with 있다/없다.
Common action in stores.
Used as a determiner or noun.

vocabulary.translation: to be uncomfortable, to cause inconvenience
vocabulary.note: Expresses physical or mental discomfort.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 이 제품에 고장이 났어요. 바꾸고 싶어요.
dialogue.translation: This product is broken. I want to exchange it.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 죄송합니다. 영수증을 확인해 주시겠어요?
dialogue.translation: I'm sorry. Could you show me the receipt?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 네, 여기 있어요. 그리고 돈도 다시 받을 수 있어요?
dialogue.translation: Yes, here it is. And can I also get my money back?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 문제 없어요. 새것으로 바꿔 드릴게요.
dialogue.translation: No problem. I'll exchange it for a new one.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 아, 불편하게 해서 죄송해요. 다음에는 잘 확인할게요.
dialogue.translation: Oh, I'm sorry for the inconvenience. Next time I'll check carefully.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 괜찮아요. 다음에 또 오세요!
dialogue.translation: It's okay. Please come again!

key_phrases.translation: Could you show me the receipt?

scenario: Booking a table at a restaurant by phone
frequency_note: words ranked ~300–700 by frequency of Korean

vocabulary.note: Regular verb, used with a direct object (e.g., 식당을 예약하다).
Functions as a time adverb.
Can also mean 'evening'.
Used with counters, e.g., 몇 시, 몇 명.
Counter for people.
Connector of cause and consequence.
Adjective used with -ㄹ 수 있어요, etc.
Although it appears in the list of words to avoid, it is necessary for the context and is not repeated in the same file.
Polite form: 알겠습니다. Used to confirm.
Compound verb of 전화 (phone) + 하다.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 여보세요, 오늘 저녁에 예약하고 싶은데요.
dialogue.translation: Hello, I'd like to make a reservation for tonight.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 네, 몇 분이세요?
dialogue.translation: Yes, how many people?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 두 명이요. 그래서 가능한 시간을 알고 싶어요.
dialogue.translation: Two people. So, I'd like to know if there's a possible time.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 네, 가능합니다. 몇 시로 할까요?
dialogue.translation: Yes, it's possible. What time would you like?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 일곱 시로 주세요. 다음에 전화할 때는 더 일찍 할게요.
dialogue.translation: Seven o'clock, please. Next time I call, I'll do it earlier.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 알겠습니다. 예약 완료했습니다.
dialogue.translation: Understood. Your reservation is confirmed.

key_phrases.translation: I'd like to make a reservation

scenario: Describing symptoms at a pharmacy
frequency_note: words ranked ~300–700 by frequency of Korean

vocabulary.note: Adjectival verb expressing pain or general discomfort.
Also means 'hair'. In medical context it refers to the head.
Used in '목이 아프다' (sore throat).
Literally 'heat'. '열이 나다' means to have a fever.

vocabulary.translation: to come out, to appear, to have (a symptom)
vocabulary.note: Used in expressions like '열이 나다' (to have a fever), '기침이 나다' (to cough).
General term for medicines.
Honorific form of '마시다' (to drink). Used with patients to show respect.
Used in '주사를 맞다' (to receive an injection).

vocabulary.translation: to receive (a blow, injection), to be correct
vocabulary.note: In this context, '주사를 맞다' = to receive an injection.
Connector indicating that something happens despite what was said before.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 약사: 어서 오세요. 어디가 아프세요?
dialogue.translation: Pharmacist: Welcome. Where does it hurt?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 환자: 머리와 목이 아프고, 열도 나요.
dialogue.translation: Patient: My head and throat hurt, and I also have a fever.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 약사: 그럼 감기 약을 드세요. 그래도 열이 계속 나면 주사를 맞아야 해요.
dialogue.translation: Pharmacist: Then take cold medicine. Even so, if the fever continues, you will need to get an injection.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 환자: 네, 알겠습니다. 약은 어떻게 먹어요?
dialogue.translation: Patient: Yes, I understand. How do I take the medicine?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 약사: 하루에 세 번, 식사 후에 드세요. 그래도 안 낫으면 병원에 가세요.
dialogue.translation: Pharmacist: Take it three times a day, after meals. Even so, if you don't get better, go to the hospital.

key_phrases.translation: Where does it hurt? / What's wrong?

scenario: Talking about your hometown to a visitor

Common noun for sea.
Common noun for mountain.

Adverb of frequency.

Common noun.
Regular verb.
Demonstrative pronoun for place.
Causal connector.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 고향이 어디예요?
dialogue.translation: Where is your hometown?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 저는 작은 해변 마을에서 살아요. 바다가 아주 가까워요.
dialogue.translation: I live in a small seaside town. The sea is very close.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 좋네요! 그런데 거기는 조용해요?
dialogue.translation: That's nice! But, is it quiet there?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 네, 조용하고 사람들이 친절해요. 그래서 자주 가고 싶어요.
dialogue.translation: Yes, it's quiet and the people are kind. So I want to go often.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 여기에서 고향까지 얼마나 걸려요?
dialogue.translation: How long does it take from here to your hometown?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 차로 두 시간쯤 걸려요. 그런데 산도 있어서 경치가 좋아요.
dialogue.translation: It takes about two hours by car. But there are also mountains, so the scenery is nice.

scenario: Changing a reservation at a hotel
frequency_note: words ranked ~300–700 by frequency of Korean

vocabulary.note: Common noun for hotel, restaurant, etc. reservations.
Verb to change a reservation, plan, etc. More formal than '바꾸다'.
Refers to the calendar date.

Predicative adjective: '가능합니다' (it is possible).
Used to check information.
Time adverb: 'already' in the sense of 'before now'.
Dependent noun used with '있다/없다' to express ability or possibility.
Connector indicating cause and effect.
Refers to an employee of a company or establishment.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 안녕하세요, 예약을 변경하고 싶은데요.
dialogue.translation: Hello, I would like to change my reservation.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 네, 예약 번호를 확인해 주시겠어요?
dialogue.translation: Yes, could you confirm the reservation number?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 네, 그런데 날짜를 다음 주로 변경할 수 있나요?
dialogue.translation: Yes, but can I change the date to next week?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 잠시만요. 그 날짜에 방이 이미 예약되어 있어서 가능하지 않습니다.
dialogue.translation: Just a moment. For that date, the room is already reserved, so it is not possible.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 그래서 다른 날짜는 없어요?
dialogue.translation: So, is there no other date?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 죄송합니다. 저희 직원이 다시 확인해 드릴게요.
dialogue.translation: I'm sorry. Our staff will check again for you.

key_phrases.translation: I would like to change my reservation

key_phrases.phrase: 날짜를 다음 주로 변경할 수 있나요?
key_phrases.translation: Can I change the date to next week?

vocabulary.translation: to be okay / to be acceptable
vocabulary.note: Very common adjective used to express that something is good or suitable.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 이것은 어때요? 가격도 괜찮고 인기 있어요.
dialogue.translation: How about this? The price is reasonable and it's popular.

dialogue.speaker: A

dialogue.translation: But that looks a bit expensive, is it okay?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 그럼 이 가격에 괜찮은 선물을 살 수 있을까요?
dialogue.translation: Then, can I buy a good gift at this price?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 물론이죠. 이 가게에서 추천하는 것은 모두 괜찮아요.

scenario: Talking about past holidays

vocabulary.note: Used as an adjective, e.g., '지난 주말' = 'last weekend'.
Common for leisure or business trips.

Used with 좋다/나쁘다 to describe the weather.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 네, 정말 좋았어요. 그런데 날씨가 조금 안 좋았어요.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 어디에 갔어요? 사진도 찍었어요?

dialogue.speaker: B

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 그런데 날씨가 안 좋았는데 사진은 잘 나왔어요?
dialogue.translation: But if the weather was bad, did the photos come out well?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 네, 정말 잘 나왔어요. 여행이 정말 재미있었어요.
dialogue.translation: Yes, they came out really well. The trip was really fun.

scenario: Discussing what you did last weekend

dialogue.speaker: A

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 토요일에 친구를 만나서 영화를 봤어요.
dialogue.translation: On Saturday I met a friend and watched a movie.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 영화는 어땠어요?
dialogue.translation: How was the movie?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 조금 재미없었어요. 그래서 일요일에는 집에서 혼자 시간을 보냈어요.

key_phrases.translation: How did you spend your weekend?

scenario: Planning a birthday party
frequency_note: words ranked ~300–700 by frequency of Korean

vocabulary.note: Used with a direct object: 친구를 초대하다.
Loanword from English 'party'.
Used to prepare something concrete (food, party, etc.).
General term for 'food' or 'meal'.
Used to indicate company: 같이 가다 (to go together).
Literally 'day of birth'.
Loanword from English 'cake'.
Used with 있다/없다: 재미있다 (fun), 재미없다 (boring).
Used to refer to the next in order or time: 다음 주 (next week).
Used with 세우다 (to make a plan) or 있다/없다.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 생일 파티 계획이 있어요?
dialogue.translation: Do you have a plan for the birthday party?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 아직 없어요. 우리 같이 음식과 케이크를 준비할까요?
dialogue.translation: Not yet. Shall we prepare the food and cake together?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 좋아요. 그런데 친구들을 몇 명 초대할 거예요?
dialogue.translation: Okay. But how many friends are you going to invite?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 다섯 명 정도요. 그리고 다음 주 토요일에 하면 재미있겠어요.
dialogue.translation: About five. And it would be fun to do it next Saturday.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 좋아요. 그럼 우리 모두 같이 준비해요.
dialogue.translation: Okay. Then let's all prepare together.

scenario: Asking about public transport routes

dialogue.translation: Excuse me, where do I have to take the bus to go to city hall?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 저 건너편 정류장에서 타세요. 그다음에 3번 버스를 타고 시청역에서 내리세요.

dialogue.speaker: B

dialogue.speaker: A

key_phrases.translation: to get off at the station

Indicates relative future time.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 내일 오전에 시간 있어? 약속이 하나 있는데 같이 갈래?
dialogue.translation: Do you have time tomorrow morning? I have an appointment, do you want to come with me?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 아마 괜찮을 것 같아. 그런데 어디로 가야 해?
dialogue.translation: It will probably be fine. But, where do I have to go?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 먼저 은행에 가고, 그리고 점심을 같이 먹자.
dialogue.translation: First, let's go to the bank, and then let's have lunch together.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 좋아! 그래서 몇 시에 만날까?
dialogue.translation: Good! So, what time shall we meet?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 오전 열 시는 어때? 그 후에 점심 먹고 나중에 커피도 마시자.
dialogue.translation: How about 10 in the morning? After having lunch, let's have coffee later.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 완전 좋아! 그럼 내일 오전에 만나.
dialogue.translation: Sounds great! Then see you tomorrow morning.

key_phrases.translation: Do you want to go together?

scenario: Complaining politely about a problem
frequency_note: words ranked ~300–700 by frequency of Korean

vocabulary.note: Used to refer to a problem or inconvenience.
Polite form of 'to say' (from 말하다). Used to address someone with respect.
Common verb for 'check'.
Adjective indicating that something arrives late or is done late.

vocabulary.translation: to be sorry, to be apologetic (expressing apologies)
vocabulary.note: Adjective form of apologizing. Frequently used as '죄송합니다' (I'm sorry).
Verb for changing something.
Adverb of repetition.
Used to express surprise that something has already happened.
Used in negative sentences or to indicate that something has not happened.
Connector to contrast or introduce an objection.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 실례지만, 방에 문제가 있어서 말씀드리고 싶어요.
dialogue.translation: Excuse me, I have a problem with the room and I wanted to mention it to you.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 네, 어떤 문제인지 말씀해 주세요. 확인해 볼게요.
dialogue.translation: Yes, please tell me what the problem is. I'll check it.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 에어컨이 벌써 고장이 났어요. 그리고 방이 아직 너무 더워요.
dialogue.translation: The air conditioner has already broken down. And the room is still too hot.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 죄송합니다. 그런데 오늘은 수리 기사님이 늦게 오실 거예요.
dialogue.translation: I'm sorry. But the technician will come late today.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 그럼 다른 방으로 바꿀 수 있을까요?
dialogue.translation: Then, could I change to another room?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 네, 가능합니다. 다시 확인하고 연락드리겠습니다.
dialogue.translation: Yes, it's possible. I'll check again and contact you.

key_phrases.translation: I have a problem and I wanted to mention it to you
Could I change to another room?

scenario: Talking about a recent film or book
frequency_note: words ranked ~300–700 by frequency of Korean

vocabulary.note: In this context, '보고' refers to a review or critique of a movie/book.
Common noun for 'movie'.
Common noun for 'book'.
Used to express that something is entertaining or interesting.
Refers to the plot or narrative of a movie/book.
Main character of the story.
Intransitive verb indicating the end of something.
Adverb of quantity, used to modify adjectives or verbs.
Adverb that intensifies a statement.
Connector that introduces a contrast or topic change.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 어제 본 영화 보고 정말 재미있었어요.
dialogue.translation: The review of the movie I saw yesterday was very interesting.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 그 영화 이야기가 조금 어땠어요? 주인공이 누구였어요?
dialogue.translation: How was the story of that movie? Who was the protagonist?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 이야기는 좋았는데, 주인공이 너무 슬프게 끝나서 조금 아쉬웠어요.
dialogue.translation: The story was good, but the protagonist ended very sadly, so it was a bit disappointing.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 그런데 책을 읽으면 더 재미있을까요?
dialogue.translation: But, would it be more interesting if I read the book?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 정말 그런 것 같아요. 책이 더 자세하니까요.
dialogue.translation: I really think so. Because the book is more detailed.

key_phrases.translation: movie review (or 'movie report', in informal context)

scenario: At a job interview (basic)
frequency_note: words ranked ~300–700 by frequency of Korean

vocabulary.note: Used to talk about previous professional experience.
Common in employment and admission contexts.
Literally 'introduction of oneself'.
Idiomatic expression: 'to enter the heart'.
It is distinguished from '물어보다' (to ask) because it is the noun.
More formal than '대답'.
Used for life experiences, not only work-related.

vocabulary.translation: to like, to love (to feel affinity)
vocabulary.note: Unlike '좋다', this verb requires a subject who feels the liking.
Functions as a predicative adjective.
Often combined with '있다' to express confidence (자신 있다).

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 안녕하세요. 먼저 자기소개 부탁드립니다.
dialogue.translation: Hello. First, please introduce yourself.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 안녕하세요. 저는 3년 동안 마케팅 경력이 있습니다. 이 회사에 지원하게 되어 기쁩니다.
dialogue.translation: Hello. I have 3 years of experience in marketing. I am glad to apply to this company.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 좋습니다. 그럼 질문이 있습니다. 어떤 일을 가장 좋아합니까?
dialogue.translation: Good. Then I have a question. What kind of work do you like the most?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 저는 팀과 함께 일하는 경험을 좋아합니다. 그리고 새로운 아이디어를 만드는 것을 즐깁니다.
dialogue.translation: I like the experience of working with a team. And I enjoy creating new ideas.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 훌륭합니다. 마지막으로, 이 직업에 자신이 필요하다고 생각합니까?
dialogue.translation: Excellent. Lastly, do you think confidence is necessary for this job?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 네, 자신 있습니다. 제 답변을 통해 저를 잘 보여드리고 싶습니다.
dialogue.translation: Yes, I have confidence. I want to show myself well through my answers.

scenario: Discussing food preferences at dinner
frequency_note: words ranked ~300–700 by frequency of Korean

vocabulary.translation: to be so, to be that way

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 이 음식 맛이 어때요? 같이 먹어 볼까요?
dialogue.translation: How is the taste of this food? Shall we try it together?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 저는 이 맛을 잘 몰라요. 조금만 주세요.
dialogue.translation: I don't know this taste well. Give me just a little.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 네, 여기 있어요. 더 드시겠어요? 아니면 싫어요?
dialogue.translation: Yes, here it is. Would you like more? Or do you dislike it?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 더는 괜찮아요. 그런데 이건 조금 매워요. 그렇지 않아요?
dialogue.translation: I don't need more. But this is a bit spicy. Isn't it?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 맞아요, 조금 매워요. 그렇지만 맛있어요. 또 먹고 싶어요.
dialogue.translation: That's right, it's a bit spicy. But it's delicious. I want to eat more again.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 저도 알겠어요. 그럼 같이 더 먹어요!
dialogue.translation: I understand too. Then let's eat more together!

scenario: Asking for help with a computer issue
frequency_note: words ranked ~300–700 by frequency of Korean

vocabulary.note: Loanword from English 'computer'.
Regular verb ending in -하다.
Used to turn on electronic devices.
Used in contexts of situation or condition of something.
Often used with -을/를 알다 (to know how).

vocabulary.translation: to let know, to notify, to inform
vocabulary.note: Compound form of 알다 (to know) + 주다 (to give).
Opposite of 켜다.
Irregular adjective: 어려운 (attributive form).
Very common adverb of manner.
Compound of 돕다 (to help) + 주다 (to give).

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 컴퓨터가 안 켜져서 너무 어려워요.
dialogue.translation: The computer won't turn on, it's very difficult.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 어떤 상태예요? 잘 사용하고 있었는데 갑자기 꺼졌어요?
dialogue.translation: What state is it in? Were you using it fine and it suddenly turned off?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 네, 껐다가 다시 켰는데 화면이 안 나와요. 방법을 알려주실 수 있어요?
dialogue.translation: Yes, I turned it off and turned it back on, but the screen doesn't come on. Can you tell me the method?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 그럼 전원을 완전히 끄고 다시 켜 보세요. 그래도 안 되면 제가 도와줄게요.
dialogue.translation: Then turn it off completely and turn it back on. If it still doesn't work, I'll help you.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 감사합니다! 그런데 완전히 끄는 방법을 잘 모르겠어요.
dialogue.translation: Thank you! But I don't really know how to turn it off completely.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 전원 버튼을 5초 동안 누르면 꺼져요. 그다음에 다시 켜면 돼요.
dialogue.translation: Press and hold the power button for 5 seconds and it will turn off. Then turn it back on.

key_phrases.translation: Turn off and turn back on

scenario: Renting an apartment (first inquiry)
frequency_note: words ranked ~300–700 by frequency of Korean

vocabulary.note: Refers to a room, but in a housing context it can mean 'apartment' or 'room'.
Regular verb, used to search for something specific.

vocabulary.translation: how is it? / what do you think?
vocabulary.note: Conjugated form of '어떻다' (to be a certain way), used in opinion questions.
Monthly rental system without a large deposit (contrast with '전세').
Used to ask about quantity or price.
Common in legal and rental contexts.
Indicates that something happens without delay or in a straight line.
Refers to the act of moving to a new home.
Literally 'owner of the house'.
Used to refer to the next thing in order or time.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 안녕하세요. 방을 찾고 있어요.
dialogue.translation: Hello. I'm looking for a room.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 네, 이 방은 어때요? 월세는 얼마예요?
dialogue.translation: Yes, how about this room? How much is the monthly rent?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 월세는 50만 원이고, 계약은 2년이에요.
dialogue.translation: The monthly rent is 500,000 won, and the contract is for 2 years.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 좋아요. 그런데 이사는 다음 주에 가능해요.
dialogue.translation: Good. But the move is possible next week.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: 그럼, 집주인에게 바로 연락할게요.
dialogue.translation: Then, I'll contact the landlord directly.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: 네, 다음에 봐요.
dialogue.translation: Yes, see you next time.

key_phrases.translation: How much is the monthly rent?
The move is possible next week.
